subject: Service Continuity Guarantee — escrowed safety pool & graduated repurchase proposal
messages:
From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>
To: marcus.lin@redwood.com, marissa.cole@acme-cc.com
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Service Continuity Guarantee — escrowed safety pool & graduated repurchase proposal

Marcus / Redwood team,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we begin legal procurement, our procurement and SRE leads have pushed back on a credits-only SLA remedy for repeated high-latency incidents given the scale of traffic we plan to route. Acme is willing to make a 12‑month committed spend, and in exchange we are asking Redwood to accept a bounded, cash-based safety mechanism beyond credits. High-level ask: 

- An "escrowed safety pool": Acme funds an escrow equal to 3 months of committed spend at contract start.
- Trigger & remedy: If monthly P95 latency exceeds the SLO threshold for 3 of 4 consecutive weeks, Acme may draw against the escrow per a graduated repurchase schedule (see table below). Draws reduce the escrow balance; Redwood has a cure window prior to payment.
- Caps & taper: Maximum cumulative draw = 6 months committed spend. Escrow replenishment optional on renewal.
- Measurement: We prefer latency measured on route 'api.redwood/v1/generate' scoped to Acme tenant, using Redwood telemetry (we can accept a neutral auditor if necessary).

Example repurchase schedule (illustrative):
- Severity A (P95 > SLO + 200ms for 3/4 weeks): draw = 25% monthly committed fee
- Severity B (P95 > SLO + 100ms for 3/4 weeks): draw = 10% monthly committed fee

We recognize this is nonstandard; if Redwood would rather offer a capped cash buyback instead of an escrow, please indicate the maximum liability you can accept and any operational constraints. We would also need a confirmation of proof-of-funds / escrow agent and a short term-sheet. Attached is a small usage snapshot to help calibrate numbers.

Would appreciate a quick confirmation today whether Redwood can entertain this structure so we can prioritize internal approvals.

Thanks,
Jane Doe
Sr. Procurement Manager, Acme Corp
attachments: usage_snapshot_Q1.csv
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rachel_kim@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Service Continuity Guarantee — escrowed safety pool & graduated repurchase proposal

Jane — thanks for the clear write-up and for sharing the snapshot. We appreciate the seriousness of Acme's request and the commitment you're offering. High-level response: Redwood is open to a bounded, cash-centric remedy in parallel with credits, but we'll need to structure it to preserve predictable risk and operational fairness across customers. A few immediate points and questions: 

1) We can consider an escrowed safety pool or a capped cash buyback. Our legal/finance typically prefers a capped-liability model with severity tiers, cure periods, and objective measurement.

2) Measurement & scope: we need to agree exact metric (P95 latency on tenant-scoped API path), sampling period, and which versions/regions are in-scope. If you need a neutral auditor for dispute windows, we can accept that with pre-agreed log exports.

3) Cure & remediation: Redwood asks for a 7-business-day remediation/cure window after an incident before a draw is allowed, to permit routing/patch actions.

4) Caps: we can accept a maximum cumulative cash exposure capped at a multiple of committed monthly spend (we typically work 1–6x depending on tier). Please confirm Acme's preferred cap (you proposed 6x months).

5) Operationally: escrow under a neutral custodian adds complexity (set-up time, legal review). For speed we can provide a term-sheet for a short-form addendum that supports either (A) escrow held by bank/custodian, or (B) Redwood-hosted reserve (segregated liability) with similar payout rules.

I've attached a one-page term summary draft to kick off redlines. Also cc'ing Marissa (sales lead) to sync pricing impacts, and Rachel (finance) for exposure modeling. To help us size any acceptable cap, could you share the last 3 months of committed billings (or confirm the committed monthly amount)? That will let us propose a single-number cap rather than a range.

If Acme is comfortable, we'll draft a short mutual action plan and circulate a redlineable term sheet by COB tomorrow.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | marcus.lin@redwood.com
attachments: RiskPool_TermSheet_v1.pdf
From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>

Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Service Continuity Guarantee — escrowed safety pool & graduated repurchase proposal

Marcus / Marissa —

Thanks for the quick reply. Per your points:

- Measurement: Agreed to tenant-scoped P95 on the 'generate' route (regionalized; we only route to us-west). We can accept Redwood telemetry with 5-business-day export windows for audit.
- Cure window: 7 business days is acceptable.
- Cap: Acme's preferred cap is 6 months committed spend (we proposed 6x to match business risk). If Redwood can only accept a lower multiplier, we need a clear trade (e.g., longer escrow term or stricter routing SLAs).
- Escrow: preference is neutral custodian (we can propose our bank's escrow agent) but a Redwood-segregated reserve is acceptable if Redwood can provide monthly balance statements and a simple draw process.

Attached is a slightly expanded usage snapshot and our committed monthly spend figure (redacted in this thread — full numbers in the attachment). Proposed timeline: sign term addendum within 10 business days to align with procurement cycle.

If you can circulate a redlineable addendum that shows both paths (custodian escrow vs Redwood reserve) + the measurement and draw mechanics, we'll route it through legal.

Thanks — Jane
Jane Doe
Sr. Procurement Manager, Acme Corp

Subject: Re: Service Continuity Guarantee — escrowed safety pool & graduated repurchase proposal

Jane — appreciate the clarity and the committed timeline. Next steps from Redwood: 

1) We'll circulate a redlineable short-form addendum today that includes two options: (A) neutral-custodian escrow; (B) Redwood segregated reserve. The addendum will include: scope (tenant/API path/region), measurement definition, 7-business-day cure, graduated draw schedule (severity tiers), cap (we'll show a 3x and 6x example), and replenishment/renewal mechanics.

2) Rachel will run the exposure model and confirm whether we can accept 6x for the initial term or whether we need a lower multiplier with additional operational commitments.

3) Marissa will update the commercial sheet to reflect any potential uplift for accepting capped cash liability (will include an optional escrow setup fee if you choose the custodian path).

4) Links: I've added the deal to HubSpot and attached a DocuSign preview link for the term addendum once redlines are agreed: https://hubspot.com/deals/ACME-2319 and https://app.docusign.com/preview/ACME-2319-term-sheet

If Acme has named signatories for finance/legal who should be included in the redline cycle, please share emails. We'll aim to have a draft on your desk today for 48-hour review.

Best regards,
Marcus Lin
